title: Block coalescing checkpointing and fine-grained GPU OOB eviction
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a paged/blocked KV cache implementation that reduces GPU OOMs and tail latency by (1) coalescing small KV fragments into block-aligned checkpointable units, (2) enabling low-latency out-of-band (OOB) evictions under memory pressure, and (3) integrating with continuous batching so batch reservation and residency behave predictably.
proposal_summary: Introduce a block descriptor layer that maps variable-length KV entries onto fixed-size slab blocks (default 256KB). Maintain a compact residency bitmap and a host-backed checkpoint store for evicted blocks. Add an asynchronous OOB eviction path that runs at <1ms decision latency when free memory falls below a hysteresis threshold. Coordinate block-level locks with the serving runtime to avoid stalls during batch hot-paths.
implementation_details: Data structures: BlockDescriptor[] with fields (block_id, slot_count, last_access_epoch, bucket_fingerprint) stored in a contiguous host/GPU-resident metadata buffer. ResidencyBitmap is a compact bitset replicated between host and device; GPU can query a small device-local cache of hot bitmaps. Checkpointing: Evicted blocks are serialized into a host pinned checkpoint ring that supports batched async DMA uploads/downloads. Eviction policy: watermarks (80%/65%) with per-model resident budgets and token-affinity scoring. OOB eviction path: fast heuristic that selects victim blocks based on stale epochs and low token-affinity, attempts to write back to host checkpoint ring using pre-allocated pinned buffers, then marks device pages free. Integration with continuous batching: batches allocate a soft reservation from model budget; blocks that are under active reservation are exempt from OOB eviction for the life of the batch. On mem pressure, continuous batching controller can reduce batch size or fallback to compatible smaller quantized model variant. Telemetry: track block hit-rate, eviction latency, checkpoint roundtrip time, OOM occurrences, and the number of batches throttled due to memory. APIs: expose per-model resident_budget and eviction_mode (eager|lazy|oob-only), and a /debug endpoint to snapshot residency and checkpoint ring state.
safety_and_consistency: Atomicity: Block eviction marks go through a 2-phase commit: (1) mark 'evicting' in metadata, (2) flush KV payload to host checkpoint ring, (3) commit 'evicted' and free device pages. Crash recovery replays pending checkpoint entries at startup. Fallback: If checkpoint ring is saturated, eviction backs off and triggers runtime-level degradation (batch size reduction and model fallback). Rollback: On failed checkpoint writes, the block remains pinned and we raise a soft OOM alarm for operator intervention.
tests_and_validation: Microbenchmarks: synthetic hotset with variable fragment sizes to verify coalescing improves GPU-residency efficiency. End-to-end: run continuous-batching workload traces (prod-sampled) with and without OOB eviction, measure 99th latency, per-token cost, and OOM rate. Chaos: force DMA stalls and verify eviction backoff triggers safe fallback. Load tests: per-model stress to validate residency budgets and cross-model isolation.
rollout_plan: Feature-gated rollout. Stage 1: internal canary on staging with low-traffic models. Stage 2: opt-in on dedicated clusters for customers testing private deployment. Stage 3: default enabled for runtime-1.21 with telemetry gating and an on-call runbook. Provide 'eviction=off' knob for immediate opt-out.
success_metrics: Reduce device-side OOMs by >=90% on long-tail workloads, improve resident block utilization by 20% (fewer small fragment overheads), keep 99th-percentile generation latency increase <5% compared to baseline, and reduce per-token device memory cost by >10% for oversubscribed clusters.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Checkpoint ring saturation leading to stalls. Mitigation: dynamic ring sizing and immediate fallback to smaller batch / model variant; operator alerts. Risk: Incorrect block coalescing causing increased read amplification. Mitigation: hybrid strategy that limits coalescing depth for high-turnover keys and adds sampling-based heuristics. Risk: GPU metadata sync overhead. Mitigation: device-local hot-bitmap caching and asynchronous diff propagation.
